title: A uniform ideal power annihilates sheaf Koszul cohomology
statement: Let C be a small site, R a sheaf of commutative rings, r a natural number, f a family of r global sections, and n a natural number. For the positive-power cochain Koszul complex K_n of [def-weil-pbc-extended-localization-cech], fix any integer q and site object X. Let I_X be the ideal generated by the values f_j(X) in R(X). Every element a of I_X^(r*(n+1)+1) annihilates every local section x of the cohomology sheaf H^q(K_n) over X. These are sections of the cohomology sheaf; cohomology need not commute with sections. The positive exponent is uniform on all site objects, including r=0.

proof.text: In degree q+1, define h_j by removing j with coefficient (-1) to the number of indices less than j, and by zero on subsets not containing j. Erasing a member lowers the cardinality by one, so this is a map to degree q. The finite coproduct universal property gives an actual module-sheaf morphism.

source.place: Tag 0626; complementary-basis cochain convention of Tag 0913

proof.text: Check d h_j + h_j d on each summand. If j is absent, only insertion of j survives, with square of the sign equal to one. If j is present, removal followed by reinsertion of j gives the diagonal scalar f_j^(n+1). For k distinct from j, compare the two orders: if k<j insertion raises the removal position by one; if j<k removal lowers the insertion position by one. The two coefficients sum to zero. Erase-insert identities identify the corresponding summands, proving the identity in all integer degrees.

Use Homotopy.nullHomotopicMap' to assemble the contraction into a null-homotopic endomorphism of the Koszul complex. The previous identity identifies every component with the diagonal scalar map. Homotopy.homologyMap_eq identifies the induced map with zero.

For a compatible global section s and an exponent e, define a natural endomorphism z of the identity functor on module sheaves by multiplication by s(X)^e on each local section module. The restriction maps are semilinear and s is compatible, proving that these are sheaf morphisms. Linearity of module morphisms proves naturality in the module. On the ring unit this endomorphism is scalar(s)^e, proved by induction using commutativity. Naturality with the coproduct injections identifies z on a free term with the diagonal matrix. Naturality with the cycles inclusion and the epimorphic homology projection identifies the induced map on homology with z on homology. Applying the null-homotopy and evaluating on X and x proves the asserted annihilation.

For a finite set s and an ideal A containing the e-th power of each generator, prove span(s)^(card(s)*e+1) <= A by induction on s. For the empty set, the zero ideal to the first power is zero. On inserting j, rewrite the span as the supremum of the singleton ideal and the previous span. Apply Ideal.sup_pow_add_le_pow_sup_pow at exponents e and card(s)*e+1. The singleton power is spanned by f_j^e and lies in A; the other term lies in A by induction. For each object X apply this bound with e=n+1 and A the annihilator ideal of the R(X)-module H^q(K_n)(X), using the generator annihilation already proved. The full finite set Fin r has cardinality r, giving the claimed uniform positive exponent.

lean.statement:
theorem koszul_ideal_power_annihilates_homology
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (r : ℕ)
    (f : Fin r → (unit (rings R)).sections) (n : ℕ) :
    ∀ (q : ℤ) (X : Cᵒᵖ) (a : R.obj.obj X),
      a ∈ (Ideal.span (Set.range (fun j : Fin r ↦
        (show R.obj.obj X from (f j).val X)))) ^ (r * (n + 1) + 1) →
      ∀ (x : ((koszul R r f n).homology q).val.obj X), a • x = 0
